The stock has been trading within a 36% range of its 52-week high and low [E5], indicating stability in recent price movements. The company's Return on Equity (ROE) is at 7.6% [E7], which is below the sector median of 22.1% [E58]. However, its compounded profit growth over the same period stands at 43% [E11], which is significantly higher and suggests that the company's profitability is on an upward trajectory. This accelerated profit growth has been driven by margin expansion, as evidenced by the increase in quarterly operating margins from -2% to 3% [E20]. Despite these positive indicators, AGARWALFT faces challenges with its compounded profit growth over three years at -17% [E12] and its trailing twelve months (TTM) profit growth at -52% [E13], which are both negative. These figures suggest that the company is currently experiencing significant profitability declines. The sector median profit growth stands at 22.1% [E58], indicating that AGARWALFT's performance in this regard is lagging behind its peers, but not by a wide margin. The fact that the stock price has grown faster than earnings over the past year (PRICE-LED) [E44] suggests that investors are expecting future growth and may be pricing in some positive surprises. In conclusion, AGARWALFT appears to be undervalued based on its current P/E ratio of 19.4 [E1], despite facing challenges with negative profit growth over the past year. The company's strong compounded sales growth and margin expansion suggest that it has significant potential for future profitability improvements. While its TTM profit growth is negative, the sector median profit growth is also negative, indicating that AGARWALFT may be better positioned than some of its peers in terms of profitability growth. The compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months is -52% [E13], which is an alarming indicator given the company's sector median profit growth at 22.1% [E58]. This suggests that AGARWALFT may be lagging its peers, potentially due to operational inefficiencies or external factors impacting profitability. Moreover, the compounded profit growth over three years has also declined sharply from a positive 43% [E11] to -17% [E12], indicating a significant downturn in earnings momentum. This decline is further exacerbated by the operating margin falling by 4 percentage points to 6% in Mar 2026 [E19], compared to 10% three years earlier, suggesting ongoing challenges in cost management and operational efficiency. The bear case also includes evidence that the stock price growth has outpaced profit growth recently. The recent period shows a 18% increase in price relative to profit growth [E44], indicating expectations may be running ahead of actual delivery. This suggests market sentiment might be overestimating future profitability, which is not supported by current financial metrics. In conclusion, the evidence points towards declining profitability and lackluster performance, making it clear that AGARWALFT's valuation does not support its current price level.
